reading: The exact human P04062 sequence occupies AN30/PTN002476139 and is identical across the official 536-residue record, cluster FASTA and ungapped MSA.

Both incoming IBA assertions descend from actual AN7/PTN001667738: glucosylceramidase activity GO0004348 and glucosylceramide catabolic process GO0006680. Every listed donor maps beneath this ancestor; literal donor sets match current incoming records, including legitimate human self-evidence.

The actual NHX ancestor species label is Eubacteria and the actual IBD GAF carries taxon2. These are preserved literally as deep-family record metadata, not interpreted as human target taxonomy or substituted for a separately demonstrated evolutionary date.

No NOT/IRD/IKR assertion appears among retained family records. Target sequence preserves the two UniProt-annotated catalytic glutamates; alignment columns and donor residues are retained without inferring equivalent assays for every family member.

These specific ancestral assertions support conserved glucosylceramide hydrolysis and catabolism. They do not by themselves establish all reported alternative substrates, compartments, clinical phenotypes or truncated-product activities.
limitations: Mechanical ancestry and sequence replay do not replace primary-study reading.

review_changes.before: Authentic abstract reports a neuronal setting with reduced GCase activity but no measured alpha-synuclein or lysosomal phenotype. This is a real context-dependent result, not grounds to deny direct enzyme activity or negate all other cellular studies.
review_changes.after: Selected full Methods/Results directly measure CBE-suppressed GCase activity in human SH-SY5Y and rat cortical cultures. Alpha-synuclein and lysosomal results are endpoint-, cell- and time-specific. The 2021 correction (https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0252975) replaces a Fig.6A panel with improperly removed lower beta-actin bands; it announces no revised enzyme assay or conclusion. Corrected figure pixels and raw blots were not independently reanalyzed.
